transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-11 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Priya Das (Redwood) — Raj Patel, Sofia Martinez, Noah Greene, Elena Voss (Kitefall)

Summary (auto): Candidate wants to understand unit economics and which hosting mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) hits their monthly spend target while keeping p95 latency under 400ms for 512-token prompts.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving this time out. quick intros?
[00:12] Raj: yeah hi I'm Raj, head of ML at Kitefall. we've been evaluating vendor options for inference - main ask is cost predictability.
[00:18] Noah: Noah here, CTO. budget ceiling, non-negotiable.
[00:22] Sofia: Sofia, infra. i'll be doing the benching and integration.
[00:26] Elena: Elena, security, i'll scope compliance questions.
[00:30] Maya: great. Liam and Priya from the SE side will walk through batching/cache levers and a pilot plan.
[00:38] Liam: hi all — quick note, we will talk about per-token price, batching windows, kv cache hit-rate and what Dedicated looks like for reserved capacity.

[02:05] Raj: our baseline — 1.2M tokens/day avg, spike to 4M on weekdays. 70% of calls are short prompts ~128 tokens, 30% are longer up to 1k. target is to keep monthly spend sub $40k for the feature.
[02:35] Liam: ok interesting, that token distribution matters a lot. short prompts benefit more from prefix caching and batching, longer ones will drive throughput. do you have a token histogram you can drop?
[02:50] Sofia: yes we'll share a sample later, it's anonymized already.

[04:15] Priya: on pricing, our Hosted API is usage based per-token. Dedicated flips that to reserved capacity (monthly commit) plus lower per-token accounting inside the pool. Private adds the infra/ops charge + licensing.
[04:40] Raj: right, so is Dedicated strictly cheaper per-token if we commit? we have limited headroom but can do a 12-month commit if numbers make sense.
[04:55] Liam: typically yes — with Dedicated you get predictable throughput and lower unit costs because the pool is optimized and you avoid multi-tenant overhead. the savings magnitude depends on Utilization and batching efficiency.

[06:30] Sofia: can you quantify "batching efficiency"? like how much we save if average batch size moves from 1 to 6?
[06:45] Liam: rough rule: increasing average batch size reduces GPU time per token up to a point. for transformer models we usually see 20-45% per-token cost improvement when batching short prompts aggressively and leveraging KV cache. so going 1 -> 6 could be ~35% improvement, but that assumes traffic can be batched without blowing latency SLOs.

[08:10] Raj: p95 latency target is 400ms for 512 tokens. will batching kill that?
[08:22] Liam: auto-batching is latency-aware — Redwood can set latency windows. small windows (20-40ms) still give batching benefit but less. the tradeoff is cost vs latency. we often recommend hybrid: use Hosted for low-volume unpredictable traffic, Dedicated for high steady state.

[10:05] Maya: also caching — prefix and KV cache can make subsequent calls much cheaper. e.g., for chat workflows where users re-use system prompts, cache-hit rates can cut tokenization/attn overhead by a lot.
[10:28] Raj: our product does a lot of templated prompts so cache hit could be good. what's the engineering lift to use KV cache?
[10:36] Priya: minimal — the runtime exposes simple headers to pin prefix cache; you can also use Redwood SDK which manages KV cache TTLs.

[12:12] Elena: on security, we need SOC2-plus, audit logs, SSO, and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Private deployment is preferable if we can't do KMS in hosted.
[12:30] Maya: understood. we have SOC2 docs and a VPC Private option with customer KMS. we can share network diagrams and an architecture checklist.

[13:50] Noah: if Private is viable, is the unit cost still competitive? we're worried ops + infra will blow the budget.
[14:02] Liam: Private adds infra + license overhead; unit costs depend on your hardware footprint. sometimes Dedicated is sweet spot — you get near-private economics with Redwood handling ops. but if you need air-gapped or strict residency, Private can be justified.

[15:30] Raj: any quick numbers — hosted per-token vs dedicated per-token vs private rough? ballpark is fine.
[15:40] Liam: ballpark: Hosted (on curated models) might be, say, $0.0008 per token for generation (varies by model). Dedicated spot might be $0.00045–0.0006 per token at good utilization. Private depends on your servers but operationalized ~ $0.00035–0.0007 after infra amortization. these are illustrations; we'll put exacts in the workbook.

[17:10] Sofia: what about quantization? we have smaller GPUs for edge and want int8 paths.
[17:20] Priya: our runtime supports quantized kernels; you can get ~2–3x memory reduction and some perf/cost wins. quality regressions exist — we run redwood-verified profiles per model.

[18:45] Raj: fallback behavior — if dedicated pool saturated, how does Redwood route requests?
[18:55] Liam: smart routing — we can failover to compatible Hosted variants or lower-precision models. routing policy is configurable by latency, cost, and region.

[20:10] Elena: audit logs — retention options and how detailed are they? we need request-level logs for three months for compliance.
[20:20] Maya: we offer configurable observability retention; can keep request traces, token-level cost breakdowns and model inputs for required windows. for sensitive data, Private + KMS is recommended.

[22:00] Raj: ok let's talk pilot. we want a 6-week pilot bounded by $10k cap to validate unit economics and caching. can Redwood run that?
[22:12] Maya: yes. typical pilots: we set up a dedicated-ish pool (pilot Dedicated or Hosted with reserved slices), run your traffic profile for 2–4 weeks, measure at token granularity, and then extrapolate. pilot plan also includes a bench with synthetic and real samples.

[23:45] Sofia: will pilot include KV cache priming? we can provide sample prompts to warm the cache.
[23:52] Liam: absolutely — priming is part of the bench. we can run A/B: cache-on vs cache-off to show deltas.

[25:10] Raj: how do we prevent noisy neighbors in Dedicated? we've seen other vendors degrade when someone spikes.
[25:22] Priya: Dedicated is isolated pools reserved for a customer — no noisy neighbors. we also support burst lanes if you need occasional headroom.

[27:00] Noah: SLA? p99 latency and uptime?
[27:06] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets at contract. Hosted SLA is softer but production friendly. Private has different SLA depending on deployment. we'll include SLA boilerplate in the follow-up pack.

[29:30] Sofia: integration — how quickly can we get SDK in and test? we prefer a small sandbox with sample creds.
[29:40] Liam: we can provision sandbox keys in a day once paperwork is in. bench harness usually takes 1–2 weeks to run representative traffic.

[31:10] Raj: what's the cost modeling approach? we need to understand sensitivity across cache hit-rate, batch size, and utilization.
[31:22] Liam: we'll provide a workbook that takes your token histogram, expected hit-rate, batch window, and utilization to generate expected spend. it will show best/worst-case scenarios and tipping points where Dedicated pays back.

[33:00] Elena: compliance paperwork — can you share SOC2 report and a list of subprocessors?
[33:10] Maya: yes, will attach SOC2, data processing addendum, subprocessor list. for Private KMS, we'll share architecture diagrams.

[34:45] Raj: sample cadence: if pilot shows 30% saving due to caching+batching, we can escalate to a 12-month commit. if it's only 5%, we stay on Hosted. that is our decision rubric.

[36:00] Liam: that makes sense. we'll also include quantization scenarios in the workbook to show marginal gains and possible quality delta.

[38:20] Sofia: latency SLO — if we need p95 < 300ms for some endpoints, can Redwood set per-route policies?
[38:30] Priya: yes, per-route SLOs and routing to low-latency pools is supported — e.g., pin to lower-latency instance type or prefer smaller batch windows.

[40:05] Noah: any gotchas on egress/residency for hosted? we host EU customers and must keep EU data in region.
[40:15] Maya: Redwood has region controls — Hosted regions in EU/US/APAC, and data residency options. Private/VPC is the strictest route.

[41:50] Raj: ok can we recap next steps?
[42:00] Maya: recap: 1) Maya will send pilot pricing and cost workbook by 2026-09-14. 2) Liam will share bench plan and a proposed Dedicated pilot config by 2026-09-16. 3) Kitefall (Sofia) to provide token histogram and 2 weeks of traffic samples by 2026-09-18. 4) Elena to list compliance must-haves and any network constraints in an email.

[43:22] Sofia: yep we'll get that over.
[43:28] Elena: and we'll expect SOC2 + ec2 diagram, thanks.

[44:10] Maya: cool — one more quick note on pricing sensitivity: small changes in batch window and cache hit-rate can swing unit costs by 20–40%, so the bench must be representative.
[44:28] Raj: good to know. thanks everyone.
[44:40] Liam: we'll email the workbook and bench plan, and suggest dates for the bench run.
[45:00] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up.

Auto-generated action snippets:
- Pilot cap requested: $10k for 6 weeks.
- Bench A/B: cache primed vs unprimed, batch windows 20/40/100ms, quantized vs full precision.

End of recording.
